Optimal.Notes: This profile balances playability and visual quality for early-to-mid game city sizes; expect frame rates to fall toward the low end or below as simulation complexity increases. In-game option names are estimated from the Unity engine and genre conventions — verify on first launch.

profiles.Summary: Cities: Skylines II is a demanding modern city builder that significantly exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities — the recommended GPU is an RTX 3080, and even the minimum (GTX 970) outclasses the Deck's RDNA 2 iGPU. Expect low frame rates, heavy CPU load from simulation, and limited playability; the game is marked Unsupported on Deck, though some ProtonDB reporters have gotten it running at reduced settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements and Steam Deck hardware capabilities. On first launch, check fps on an empty map — if it's already below 20, the game may not be viable for extended play; watch for crashes and RAM pressure as your city grows.

MaxBattery.Notes: At this profile the Deck is thermal- and power-limited; expect low fps even on an empty map, and frame rates will drop further as your city grows. GE-Proton is recommended by community reporters for better compatibility.

KnownIssues: Game is officially 'Unsupported' on Steam Deck — crashes, UI scaling issues, or launch failures may occur.
Heavy CPU simulation load causes frame drops and stuttering as city size grows, regardless of GPU settings.
16 GB shared RAM may be insufficient for large cities, leading to slowdowns or out-of-memory crashes.
UI text and menus may be very small or difficult to read at 1280x800 without UI scaling adjustments.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Even at full TDP the Deck cannot reliably sustain 30 fps on larger cities — treat the 30 fps cap as an aspirational ceiling on a fresh, small map only. Battery life will be short and thermals will be at their limit.

Optimal.Notes: This profile balances visual clarity with stability, using FSR upscaling from 1024x640 to recover sharpness while keeping GPU load manageable at 12 W. Medium LOD and volumetrics give the city a livelier look without overwhelming the RDNA 2 GPU; reduce LOD to Low if late-game cities stutter.

profiles.Summary: Cities: Skylines II is a demanding city-builder that significantly exceeds the Steam Deck's GPU capabilities even at minimum PC specs, making stable 30 fps a challenge that requires aggressive settings reductions and upscaling. The game runs via Proton (gold tier) but expect heavy CPU bottlenecks in large cities and thermal pressure at higher TDPs.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB player reports with settings details were found; all three profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck hardware capability. On your first run, test in a small early-game city and check whether 30 fps holds — if it doesn't even there, drop to the Max Battery profile and reduce city size expectations significantly.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 8 W TDP with a locked GPU clock and FSR upscaling from 960x600, the Deck can squeeze the most playtime out of a charge, though late-game large cities will push below 30 fps due to CPU simulation load. Keep cities modest in size to maintain playability.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Running at full 15 W TDP and native 1280x800 with an 85% render scale gives the best visual fidelity the Deck can realistically offer, locked to 40 fps via the OLED's 40 Hz refresh for smooth frame pacing. Expect the frame cap to be breached in large, complex cities — this is a CPU-bound simulation and no GPU setting fully compensates for that.
